growth_signal.value: No growth numbers yet, but early customers already include NVIDIA, Mistral and Fastweb, and this seed round is its first outside funding.

entry.idea: Running Kubernetes, the software that powers most cloud data centers, gets very hard once you have many clusters, so Clastix builds tools that make it simple to run and manage Kubernetes at large scale.
entry.lesson: Take a popular open-source project you built and package it into an easier, supported product that large organizations will pay for.
entry.name: Clastix

growth.reason: Too early for growth numbers, but landing customers like NVIDIA and Mistral before this being its first funding round is a positive sign.

market.reason: Managing Kubernetes at scale is a real and growing need for companies and governments, but Clastix's sovereign-Europe pitch is a niche within the huge cloud market.

tech.reason: Solid engineering built on open-source projects (Capsule and Kamaji) that a strong team could learn to use or copy in months.

entry.twist: Its platform, kMetal, combines two open-source projects it built, Capsule and Kamaji, to run many Kubernetes clusters as one fleet, and it already counts NVIDIA, Mistral and the telecom operator Fastweb as customers.
entry.who_pays: Companies and public bodies in Europe that want to run their own secure, large-scale Kubernetes infrastructure instead of renting it fully from foreign cloud giants.
entry.why_now: European governments and companies want cloud infrastructure they fully control instead of depending on big US tech firms, especially as AI computing needs grow fast.
